Flathead Catfish

Overview

The flathead catfish has a broad, flat head, with a lower jaw protruding beyond the upper jaw. Its back and sides are brown to yellow, with black-to olive-brown mottling.

Habitat

Deep, slow pools of large rivers and reservoirs, near woody cover.

Regulations

Flathead Catfish are considered nongame fish by the N.C. Wildlife Resources Commission.

Fishing Tips

Live fish, such as shad, panfish and bullhead catfish, are the preferred baits for large flathead catfish.

Places to Fish

The Cape Fear, Neuse and Lumber rivers all hold flatheads.

Management

2021 - Fisheries Resources of the Black River (26-page Final Report); 2021 - Fisheries Resources of the Cape Fear River.
